abstract: The eukaryotic nucleus has a hierarchical organization that permits genomic regulation. The genome is packaged as chromatin, which is silenced conditionally as facultative heterochromatin, or more stably silenced as constitutive heterochromatin. The smaller fractions of the genome that contain gene-rich sequences are organized into open chromatin conformations known as euchromatin. The inactive X (Xi) chromosome territory presents a uniquely powerful model system to investigate chromosome-scale gene silencing, as the entire chromosome undergoes coordinated epigenetic repression. The unique chromosome-wide silencing event provides a tractable system for investigating how molecular mechanisms of gene repression are translated into mesoscale structural features. This work builds on previous structural studies of the Xi that have leveraged conventional electron microscopy (EM) and cryo-EM, which have led to remarkable insights into the structural underpinnings of genome silencing. These approaches, however, are unable to directly distinguish chromatin from RNA and protein features. To resolve the molecular composition of the Xi chromosome territory and to provide a model of the structural organization of the chromatin, RNA and protein we analyzed the Xi using Electron Spectroscopic Imaging (ESI). We are able to resolve structural features without the use of contrast enhancing stains, using the distinct elemental signatures of chromatin, RNA and protein and combining them into composite images. By coupling ESI and electron tomography, we can circumvent the projection limitation of EM and provide an unprecedented view of the spatial organization of chromatin fibres in relation to structural features including RNA and proteins in 3D. Additionally, we employed correlative light-microscopy with ESI in physical serial sections and computationally assembled a structural model of the entire Xi chromosome territory revealing an intricate spatial network with distinct chromatin domains, distributed RNA-protein clusters, and identified a large, and previously uncharacterized mesoscale non-chromatin structure. Together, these observations provide new insights into the architecture of the Xi chromosome territory and shed electrons on the structural basis of chromosome-scale genome organization.
